announcements.text: Lockheed Martin Corp., Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Co., Fort Worth, Texas, is awarded a $330,602,692 fixed-price incentive (firm-target) modification (P00012) to a previously awarded contract (N0001925C0070). This modification adds scope to provide for long-lead materials, parts, and components in support of the production of 75 Lot 22 F-35 Lightning II aircraft for the Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps. Work will be performed in Fort Worth, Texas (59%); El Segundo, California (14%); Warton, United Kingdom (9%); Cameri, Italy (4%); Orlando, Florida (4%); Nashua, New Hampshire (3%); Baltimore, Maryland (3%); San Diego, California (2%); and other international locations (2%), and is expected to be completed in December 2030. Fiscal 2027 aircraft procurement (Air Force) funds in the amount of $80,168,692; and fiscal 2027 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $250,434,000, will be obligated at the time of award. This modification was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: BAE Systems Information and Electronics, Nashua, New Hampshire, is awarded a $104,686,379 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification (P00018) to a previously issued delivery order (N0001924F0095) against basic ordering agreement (N0001922G0009). This modification increases the order value and definitizes the effort to update the design architecture of the Advanced Survivability Pod (ASP) during its engineering and manufacturing development phase for the Navy's P-8A Poseidon aircraft. The effort supports the development and integration of ASP capabilities, including associated software and hardware upgrades. Work will be performed in Nashua, New Hampshire (91.5%); Austin, Texas (6.3%); and Patuxent River, Maryland (2.2%), and is expected to be completed in January 2030. announcements.text: Sikorsky Aircraft Corp., Stratford, Connecticut, is awarded a $10,966,825 cost-plus-fixed-fee and firm-fixed-price delivery order (N0001927F1076) against previously issued basic ordering agreement (N0001923G0002). This order provides engineering support for the design, development, integration, testing, verification, and validation of upgrades to the Onboard Inert Gas Generator System for the Marine Corps CH-53K helicopter. The effort will address obsolete components, improve electrical reliability against voltage transients, and enhance aircraft survivability while preparing the upgraded system for production integration. Work will be performed in Davenport, Iowa (52%); and Stratford, Connecticut (48%), and is expected to be completed in November 2029. Fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $10,966,825 will be obligated at the time of award. This order was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.
